entries.title: Scene
entries.definition: Action unfolding within a particular stretch of story time and space.
entries.application: Give each scene a concrete change.
entries.prompt: What is different when this scene ends?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Basic Terms

entries.title: Sequence
entries.definition: Connected scenes or shots that form a larger dramatic unit.
entries.application: Outline the unit before polishing individual scenes.
entries.prompt: What question holds these scenes together?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Basic Terms

entries.title: Mise-en-scène
entries.definition: The arrangement of the visible world before the camera: setting, performers, costume, lighting and objects.
entries.application: Choose details that reveal your world through action.
entries.prompt: Which prop changes meaning when another character touches it?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Basic Terms

entries.title: Character and action
entries.definition: A writing exercise: reveal a character through observable choices within a scene.
entries.application: Put an intention under pressure; describe the resulting behavior.
entries.prompt: What does this person do when the easy choice disappears?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Basic Terms

entries.title: Framing
entries.definition: The selection and arrangement of what appears within the image boundary.
entries.prompt: What could remain outside the frame until the reveal?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Cinematography

entries.title: Close-up
entries.definition: A tight view that emphasizes a face or another detail.
entries.application: Reserve emphasis for information the audience needs.
entries.prompt: Which small gesture carries the scene?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Cinematography

entries.title: Depth of field
entries.definition: The distance range that appears acceptably sharp in an image.
entries.application: Decide which planes of action need readable detail.
entries.prompt: Should the background action be noticed immediately?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Cinematography

entries.title: Pan
entries.definition: Horizontal rotation of a camera from its position.
entries.application: Use movement to reveal a relationship between subjects.
entries.prompt: What new information appears at the end of the pan?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Cinematography

entries.title: Tracking shot
entries.definition: A shot made while the camera travels through space.
entries.application: Consider whose movement the viewpoint follows.
entries.prompt: What changes when the camera follows rather than waits?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Cinematography

entries.title: Continuity editing
entries.definition: Shot organization that helps viewers follow space, time and action across cuts.
entries.application: Track positions and actions when revising a sequence.
entries.prompt: Can a viewer tell where everyone is after the cut?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Editing

entries.title: Crosscutting
entries.definition: Alternating between separate lines of action.
entries.application: Make the relationship between the actions intentional.
entries.prompt: Does the alternation imply simultaneity, contrast or a coming meeting?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Editing

entries.title: Eyeline match
entries.definition: An edit linking a look with the object or space being looked toward.
entries.application: Distinguish what a character notices from what the audience knows.
entries.prompt: How would delaying the reverse view change the scene?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Editing

entries.title: Montage
entries.definition: The assembly of shots; also a sequence that compresses time or builds meaning through juxtaposition.
entries.application: Specify the progression rather than a list of attractive images.
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Editing

entries.title: Diegetic sound
entries.definition: Sound belonging to the represented story world, whether its source is visible or offscreen.
entries.application: Name a sound source when it matters to the action.
entries.prompt: Who can hear the noise, and who cannot?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Sound

entries.title: Nondiegetic sound
entries.definition: Sound presented outside the story world, such as an external musical score.
entries.application: Keep audience information distinct from character knowledge.
entries.prompt: Would this moment read differently without the score?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Sound

entries.title: Sound bridge
entries.definition: Audio that connects a transition between scenes or shots.
entries.application: Use a recurring sound to establish a deliberate connection.
entries.prompt: What sound begins before its new location is shown?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Sound

entries.title: Offscreen sound
entries.definition: Sound whose source is outside the current frame.
entries.application: Let sound expand a location beyond what is visible.
entries.prompt: What unseen activity changes the meaning of this room?
caveats: The application and prompt are optional writing exercises, not production rules.

sources.title: Further reading: Yale Film Analysis — Sound
